analyticalQuestion: Does the exact multiplicative charge character omega_s=(4/5)^s move the true reduced-system threshold, which center charges create that threshold, and what geometric trade-off does the new anisotropic norm make?
supportedClaim: For the reduced canonical edge generating system with ||f||_(r,c)=sum |f_mn| r^(m+n)c^(2n-m) and c=4/5, the true s=162,j=81 column has a globally unique positive threshold root satisfying 0.382618642388680778<r_*^(4/5)<0.382618642388680779. An exact 81-polynomial Sturm sequence independently counts one root in that interval. Across [0.382618,0.382619], an exact monotone sandwich keeps all 243 competing columns and sectors below the active column; the nearest is s=164 with a strict gap approximately 1.4157274652028842093e-4. Charges q=-1 and q=+1 provide approximately 50.508% and 38.299% of the active column. Relative to the upper endpoint of the R0.48 threshold, rho_Z grows by 26.88545%, rho_W shrinks by 35.03465%, and the fixed-charge R=Z^2W disk radius gains a strict lower factor 1.0459367903514846826. The polydiscs are not nested, and no optimality or three-dimensional Navier-Stokes claim is made.
